title: Saturating Cursor Orbit
statement: Let $R$ be a natural number, let $P$ assign a finite Boolean word to each natural number, and let $F$ map finite Boolean words to finite Boolean words. Suppose that for every $j\le R+1$, applying $F$ to $P(j)$ gives $P(\min(j+1,R+1))$. Then for every natural number $i$, applying $F$ repeatedly $i$ times to $P(0)$ gives $P(\min(i,R+1))$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ maps natural numbers to finite Boolean words
$F$ maps finite Boolean words to finite Boolean words
replaced: Let $R$ be a bound, let a packing map assign a word to each cursor value, and suppose a step function sends the packed word of $i$ to the packed word of $\min(i+1, R+1)$ for every $i \le R+1$. Then for all $i$, iterating the step function $i$ times from the packed word of $0$ yields the packed word of $\min(i, R+1)$: the cursor reaches each legal round and then stalls at the one-past-last value.
